title: Cashew Chicken Chili
imagePrompt: A deep rust-brown chili fills the bowl, its sauce glossy and thick enough to cling to shredded chicken with a faint sheen from melted dark chocolate. Threads of pale, fork-shredded chicken and burgundy kidney beans break the surface, studded with pale golden cashews — some ground smooth into the sauce for body, others left whole for bite. A swirl of ivory yogurt marbles through the top and flecks of bright green cilantro rest against the dark sauce, ladled over a mound of white rice at the edge of the bowl.
subtitle: Mole-inspired ancho-chipotle chili with toasted cashews, dark chocolate, and a cool yogurt-cilantro swirl.

ingredients.heading: Ingredients
ingredients.note: Cashews do double duty here — half get blended into the purée for body, half stay whole and toasted for crunch.
items: 3 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 cups low-sodium chicken broth
⅔ cup raw cashews, divided
2 tbsp olive oil
2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs, trimmed
1 large yellow onion, chopped
4 garlic cloves, minced
1 tbsp ground cumin
1 tsp ground coriander
1 cinnamon stick (or ½ tsp ground cinnamon)
1½ tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
2 chipotle chiles in adobo, chopped, plus 1 tbsp adobo sauce
1 (14.5 oz) can diced tomatoes, with juice
1 (15 oz) can kidney beans, rinsed and drained
1 oz bittersweet chocolate, chopped
⅓ cup fresh cilantro, chopped, divided
⅓ cup plain whole-milk yogurt, for serving
Cooked white or jasmine rice, for serving
ingredients.callout: Two jobs for the cashews: a third get blended into the chile purée for silkiness, the rest stay whole and toasted, stirred in at the end for crunch.

shoppingList.item: Chipotle chiles in adobo (1 small can)

body.html: A mole-inspired chili: dried ancho chiles and chipotles in adobo are toasted and blended into a deep, chocolate-rounded purée, then simmered with chicken thighs until they shred with a fork. Toasted cashews go in twice — ground into the sauce for body, and whole for crunch — and a swirl of yogurt and cilantro cools it all down at the end.

items: Toast + blend the chile purée — anchos, chipotles, cashews, broth
Build the base — onion, garlic, warm spices
Simmer the chicken in the purée until fall-apart tender
Shred + finish with beans, chocolate, and toasted cashews
Swirl in yogurt and serve over rice

body.html: Make-ahead friendly: Flavor deepens overnight — this chili is even better the next day, and freezes well for up to 3 months.

slides.title: Toast Cashews + Make the Chile Purée
slides.checkboxLabel: Purée blended, cashews toasted and set aside

items: Toast the whole ⅔ cup cashews in a dry skillet over medium heat, shaking often, 3-4 minutes until golden and fragrant. Set aside to cool — you'll split them later.
In the same dry skillet, toast the ancho chiles a few seconds per side until pliable and fragrant.
Bring the chicken broth to a boil, then pour over the anchos in a bowl. Let soak 10 minutes until softened.
Transfer the anchos and broth to a blender with the chipotles + adobo sauce and ⅓ cup of the toasted cashews. Purée until completely smooth.

body.html: Scorched chiles turn bitter. A few seconds per side wakes up their oils — that's all you need.

items: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, 6-7 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic, cumin, coriander, cinnamon stick, and salt. Stir 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken thighs to the pot and turn to coat in the spiced onions.
Stir in the chile purée and diced tomatoes with their juice.
Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, 40-45 minutes, until the chicken is completely tender and shreds easily.

body.html: Don't rush the simmer. The purée needs the full 40 minutes to lose its raw-chile edge and turn silky.

slides.title: Shred + Finish
slides.checkboxLabel: Chicken shredded, beans + chocolate stirred in

items: Remove the chicken to a bowl (discard the cinnamon stick) and shred with two forks.
Return the shredded chicken to the pot along with the kidney beans, chocolate, and the remaining ⅓ cup toasted cashews.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, 5 minutes, until the chocolate is fully melted and everything is heated through. Taste and adjust salt.

body.html: The chocolate should disappear. It's there to round out the chile heat, not to taste like dessert — if you can taste chocolate specifically, ease up next time.

slides.title: Swirl + Serve
slides.checkboxLabel: Yogurt swirled in, plated over rice

items: Spoon the chili over cooked rice in bowls.
Swirl a spoonful of yogurt into each bowl and scatter with the remaining cilantro.
Optional toppings: sliced avocado, lime wedges, extra toasted cashews, warm tortillas
